transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start: 09:07 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Ravi (CTO), Maya (Head of ML), Jonah (Security Lead)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
Hawkeye is evaluating Redwood for an embedded payments assistant across customer support and internal ops. Primary concerns are PCI-safe tool-calling, 32k+ context summarization of transaction histories, and Spanish/Portuguese support. They want cost comparisons between hosted and dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for compliance.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone, thanks for making time, uh quick roll call, i'm ethan from Redwood, this is sofia, our solutions engineer.
[00:06] Ravi: hey ethan, hey sofia, ravi here, thanks.
[00:09] Maya: Maya on the ML team.
[00:11] Jonah: Jonah from security.
[00:13] Ethan: awesome, y'all got the agenda i sent? quick discovery, main requirements, then talk model choices, context lengths, tool-calling patterns, and security.
[00:20] Ravi: yep we did. we want to be explicit about PCI scope — we cannot have raw PAN data leave our env — that's a hard no.
[00:29] Sofia: totally understood. we've worked with several finservs on patterns — typically either tokenization + proxying calls, or we run redwood private in a vpc with HSM/KMS for key management.
[00:41] Jonah: when you say "redwood private" are you referring to the on-prem package or VPC-hosted control plane? sometimes i see mixed terms.
[00:47] Sofia: sorry, new wording is a bit messy — Redwood Private can be either customer-hosted control plane in their VPC or an on-prem appliance. the important bit is the data path and KMS integration. we can do HSM integrations for key wrapping as well.
[01:00] Maya: for the assistant we plan to summarize user transaction threads — think 20–30 messages, but combined they can be very long, like 20k to 40k tokens per session. we need good quality on longer context.
[01:12] Ethan: okay so 32k is a target, maybe sometimes 64k in peaks?
[01:16] Maya: yes 32k common, 64k occasional.
[01:19] Sofia: for long context there are tradeoffs — model choice + quantization affect latency and cost. open models like Llama variants with 32k context can be efficient on dedicated infra, but if you need deterministic SLA and simplified onboarding, our hosted API can also run optimized variants.
[01:34] Ravi: can you unpack "optimized variants"? like are those your own forks or quantized versions?
[01:39] Sofia: good question — it's a mix: we onboard community/open models and run them with runtime optimizations — better attention kernels, kv-cache handling, and we provide quantization profiles that preserve quality versus cost. sometimes we also offer curated model blobs with slight rewrites for inference efficiency — not model training, just execution artifacts.
[01:56] Jonah: you mentioned kv cache, i've heard it as "KV cash" in notes before, ha — how does caching affect PCI-sensitive data? if cached, where does it live?
[02:05] Sofia: ha — KV cash, yes. caching is per-request prefix and per-customer partitioning; in Hosted we encrypt at rest and in transit and keys are managed by us, with tenant isolation. In Private/VPC you hook into your KMS/HSM so keys never leave your control. we also support cache hot-eviction policies so you can avoid storing any PII/PAN in the cache by instructing the app layer to redact before caching.
[02:28] Ravi: that redaction approach is interesting — but it adds engineering overhead client-side. ideal is a pattern where the agent can call out to a proxied payments API to fetch last4 and status without exposing PAN. tool-calling with strict scopes.
[02:40] Ethan: we usually recommend a tool-calling pattern where the model only receives metadata returned by a backend service — the model calls a "getPaymentSummary" tool, your backend enforces PCI checks, returns masked fields like last4, status, and merchant notes. the raw PAN never goes to the model.
[02:55] Maya: ok that works. question though — do you support function/tool calling natively? we need structured output for downstream systems.
[03:02] Sofia: yes, our API supports streaming + structured function calls. small caveat: some open models need small mediators to map their outputs into strict schemas, we provide helper libraries.
[03:12] Ravi: performance and cost — if we do hosted vs dedicated — what's the break-even for 24/7 production traffic?
[03:18] Ethan: depends on qps and tokens. rough thumb rule: if you're approaching sustained hundreds of qps or large context per request (32k), dedicated reserved capacity typically wins on unit cost and predictable latency. Hosted is great early stage or spiky workloads with lower sustained qps.
[03:33] Maya: i can give ballpark — our peak is around 40 qps, average 12 qps, but tokens per request vary a lot — sometimes 10k tokens for retrieval-augmented summaries.
[03:44] Sofia: with 10k tokens per request and 40 qps peaks, we'd run cost sims but likely recommend dedicated for heavy RUs and to hit latency SLAs — we can also tranche capacity so you have base reserved plus burst.
[03:56] Jonah: for security all of our legal infra wants SOC2, ISO, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and full network diagrams. do you have those publicly?
[04:05] Ethan: yes — we'll send the security deck and runbook. we have SOC 2 and ISO docs, plus a private-only runbook for VPC/on-prem deployments.
[04:12] Ravi: are there customers in payments who did Private on prem? would appreciate a reference.
[04:16] Sofia: yes a few regional processors — i'll include redacted references.
[04:20] Maya: back to models — we care about multilingual: english is primary but spanish and portuguese support must be high quality for summarization and NER over merchant notes. do you benchmark per-language?
[04:33] Sofia: we do language-specific evals. some open models degrade in PT, ES for long-context; we often recommend an ensemble or fallback path: use a main model for EN, and a second vetted open model for ES/PT, or run a single larger multilingual model if budget allows.
[04:49] Ethan: and with routing policies you can send by language to different model variants — Redwood Console lets you route by policy (latency, cost, or language).
[04:58] Ravi: hm ok. what about hallucinations on financial facts — like the model inventing transactions? any guardrails?
[05:05] Sofia: yes, tool-calling is the primary guardrail — the model asks the getPaymentSummary tool rather than inventing amounts. we also do output scoring and can run lightweight verification layers post-generation.
[05:16] Jonah: audit logs need to show which model version produced a response, token counts, and tool call traces — can you provide token-level cost attribution?
[05:24] Ethan: that's in Redwood Console — token breakdown by model, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. snapshotting model version and trace for audit is supported.
[05:33] Maya: curious about quantization and accuracy at 32k — do you have published benchmarks? we asked another vendor and they had big perf drops at high context when quantized.
[05:42] Sofia: we have benchmarks, and we'll share a 32k vs 8k comparison for our hosted and dedicated runtimes. quantization profiles are tuned per-model; sometimes the 8-bit path performs fine, other cases 4-bit requires extra calibration. we'll include notes.
[05:55] Ravi: what's the expected latency for a 10k token generation on dedicated infra? even ballpark — 200ms per token?
[06:02] Sofia: it's variable, depends on throughput and GPU type. per-token time isn't linear at long context because attention grows; but with optimized kernels and KV streaming you can often keep tail latency reasonable — we'll run a test; rough tail for 10k generation could be tens of seconds end-to-end depending on response length. for summarization where model condenses, generation output might be much shorter than input context so it helps.
[06:23] Maya: can we do hybrid: local retrieval + run shorter prompt by extracting relevant sections before model call? that would lower token costs.
[06:29] Ethan: absolutely — retrieval and pre-filtering is a common pattern — caching embeddings for quick recalls, then send narrowed prompt. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/caching/quantization setups.
[06:40] Ravi: on legal side, we have a vendor checklist: indemnity, data residency, and the ability to sign a DPA that restricts data usage. Does Redwood have a standard DPA?
[06:50] Ethan: yes we have standard DPA, and enterprise account managers can scope additional clauses. we'll hand off to legal in the next step.
[06:57] Jonah: any concerns about model provenance? we need to track exact model artifact hashes used in production.
[07:02] Sofia: we store model build metadata and runtime artifact references, and console surfaces model version IDs. we'll include how to export hashes for your audit.
[07:09] Maya: nice. one more question: tool-calling latency limits — if the model calls backend APIs, what's the recommended timeout pattern? if backend takes 2s, do you block? queue?
[07:18] Sofia: recommend synchronous short timeouts for critical calls and async patterns for heavy ops. we support streaming partial outputs while awaiting tool responses; your backend can also provide a fast placeholder then follow up. stateful orchestration is usually handled at the app layer.
[07:31] Ethan: ok i want to recap and ensure we captured next steps — send pricing, security docs, benchmark plan, and schedule PCI deep dive. anything missing?
[07:40] Ravi: also references and a preliminary network diagram for Private option.
[07:45] Jonah: and a list of controls you can demonstrate in a POC — token logging options, redaction hooks.
[07:51] Ethan: got it. 
[07:54] Maya: sounds good. when can we run the sample benchmark?
[07:57] Sofia: i'll request a small sample from you today, then target results in a week — plan to iterate on quantization choices.
[08:06] Ethan: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with an email summarizing and attach docs.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quirks: speaker turns occasionally merged, proper nouns like "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Dedicatd", "KV cache" appears as "KV cash" or "K-V cash" in automatic captions. Some numeric tokens transcribed as words.
